method: Five Sonnet research agents; quotes re-checked against raw pages (quote_check, 1.0 = verbatim)

characters.description: Upper trunk and branches thin, flaking, orange-red; lower trunk thick grey-brown plated. Seen from distance as bright orange crown-half over dark base.
characters.quote: on upper stem and branches, thin, flaking, orange-red

characters.description: Base bark thick, scaly-plated, grey-brown, with deep fissures between plates.
characters.quote: Bark on lower stem thick, scaly-plated, grey-brown

characters.description: Plates and fissures develop with age at trunk base.
characters.quote: develops plates and fissures over time

characters.description: Young trees and pole-stage stems are thin, orange-brown and flaking all the way down; no grey plated base yet.
Resin exudates on wounds and branch stubs; pine resin smell.
Straight in forest-grown stands; bare lower trunk, crown high. Open-grown trees crooked and wide.
characters.quote: In its native areas, stem straightness is usually very good.

characters.description: Old crown dense, broadly domed or flat-topped, branches bare below; young crown conical with whorls.
characters.quote: usually eventually becoming dense, broadly domed or even flat-topped

characters.description: Needles in pairs, short, twisted, glaucous blue-green (2.5-9 cm).
characters.quote: growing in pairs on short side shoots

characters.description: Small grey-brown conic cones with raised bump on each scale.
characters.quote: a raised, circular bump at the centre of each scale

characters.description: End grain: pale yellowish sapwood, reddish-brown heartwood, visible resin canals, distinct early/late wood, strong resin smell.
Clear sapwood/heartwood contrast in cut logs; pale sapwood vs red-brown core (spruce/fir have little contrast).

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Scots pine shows orange-red flaking upper trunk; black pine bark is grey/dark throughout with thick plates, needles longer and darker.
look_alikes.quote: on upper stem and branches, thin, flaking, orange-red

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Spruce needles single on woody pegs; pine needles in pairs.
look_alikes.quote: growing in pairs on short side shoots

characters.description: Young bark coppery grey-brown, looks smooth but is rough with small papery scales; orange-brown in finely flaking form.
characters.quote: rough with papery scales

characters.description: Mature bark orange-brown to red-brown, finely flaking into small round scales.
characters.quote: Bark orange-brown, finely flaking, becoming gray-brown, scaly on old trees.

characters.description: Over ~80 years: dark purple-brown, cracked into small plates/scales. No deep ridges unlike pine.
characters.quote: dark purple-brown bark with cracks and small plates

characters.description: Amber resin droplets/crusts on trunk, wounds and stubs; fir has resin in closed blisters instead.
Tall, straight, tapering, regular whorls of branches; shallow root plate (windthrow).
characters.quote: pointed crown

characters.description: Upper branches level or ascending, lower drooping; branches in tiers with drooping twigs (var. 'pendula' habit).
characters.quote: the upper level or ascending, the lower drooping

characters.description: Narrow conical, pointed; stays pointed with age (fir flattens).
characters.quote: crown conic

characters.description: 4-angled stiff sharp needles on woody pegs; rough twig after needles fall; can roll between fingers.
characters.quote: 4-angled in cross section, rigid, light to dark green

characters.description: Long (10-16 cm) pendent cones that fall whole; ground litter of whole cones.
characters.quote: long cones which hang down from the tree

characters.description: Whitish to pale yellowish, little heartwood contrast, small pin knots, resinous smell; spruce/fir hard to separate in logs.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Spruce cones hang and fall whole; fir cones erect on branch. Fir needles flat with white stripes; spruce needles 4-angled on pegs.
look_alikes.quote: Seed cones cylindrical, attenuate at the ends, 10-16 × 3-5 cm, green when young, turning red-brown

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Young fir trunk smooth grey with resin blisters; spruce scaly red-brown.
look_alikes.quote: Bark smooth, gray, scaly, with resin blisters.

characters.description: Smooth, silvery-grey bark on young trees and upper trunk, with resin blisters.
characters.quote: Bark smooth, gray, scaly, with resin blisters.

characters.description: Raised resin blisters on young bark; pop to release clear resin. Distinctive vs spruce.
characters.quote: Bark smooth, gray, scaly, with resin blisters.

characters.description: Old bark grey to brownish, cracks into small thick rectangular plates; blisters disappear. Can be confused with old spruce.
Middle-aged bark begins flaking with irregular lifting edges.
Long clear straight bole, regular whorled horizontal branches.
characters.quote: with a long clear bole and a pyramidal crown that becomes flat-topped with age

characters.description: Old crown flat-topped (stork's nest) vs spruce staying pointed; branches spread horizontally.
characters.quote: a pyramidal crown that becomes flat-topped with age

characters.description: Flat needles in two rows with two white bands beneath, notched tip, round suction-cup scars, smooth twig.
characters.quote: Shade foliage 2-ranked, spreading horizontally; foliage in sun more or less erect.

characters.description: Erect cylindrical cones that shed scales leaving a spike on branch.
characters.quote: Seed cones cylindrical, attenuate at the ends, 10-16 × 3-5 cm, green when young, turning red-brown

characters.description: Whitish, no resin canals (unlike spruce/pine), odourless; no heartwood contrast.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Smooth grey young trunk with resin blisters = fir; scaly orange-brown with scattered resin = spruce.
look_alikes.quote: Bark smooth, gray, scaly, with resin blisters.

characters.description: Young bark thin, smooth, grey-brown with fine scales; small trunks show fissuring from approx. 10-15 yrs.
Deeply fissured, flaking, grey to reddish-brown; fissures reveal reddish inner bark.
characters.quote: Bark deeply fissured, flaking, medium to dark gray to reddish brown, with reddish inner bark.

characters.description: Thick pinkish-brown bark with wide vertical fissures and long ridges.
characters.quote: Its bark is pinkish-brown and thick, developing wide vertical fissures with age.

characters.description: Single straight round trunk with pyramidal to columnar crown, downswept branches ascending at tips.
characters.quote: usually with a single round trunk supporting a pyramidal to columnar crown of thick, downswept branches.

characters.description: Knobby short shoots (spurs) all along twigs and branches, visible in winter as bumps.
characters.quote: the stubby short shoots cylindrical and 3-10 mm long.

characters.description: Open, airy conical crown with hanging branchlets; light-coloured sparse look.
characters.quote: cone-shaped when young, becoming broad with age

characters.description: Soft light-green needles in rosettes of 30-40; turn golden yellow in autumn and fall; bare in winter.
characters.quote: in bunches of 30-40 needles, 2.5-3.5 cm long, 0.5-1 mm thick, linear, soft, pliable.

characters.description: Small ovoid cones 2.5-4 cm, persist on bare twigs for years.
characters.quote: the small oval cones that remain on the tree, and the loss of its needle-like leaves

characters.description: Pale yellow sapwood, red-brown heartwood, resinous, very dense; contrast strong, harder than spruce/pine.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Japanese larch has reddish twigs and recurved cone scales; bark overlaps, so use twigs/cones (general knowledge).
Larch sheds needles in autumn; bark lacks orange flaking crown.
look_alikes.quote: Its needles form clusters, like rosettes, along the twigs.

characters.description: Young stems golden/red-brown, turning white by sapling stage; horizontal lenticels.
characters.quote: golden-brown at first, but later this turns to white

characters.description: White papery bark with dark horizontal lenticels and black marks; peels in thin sheets. Decisive for genus.
characters.quote: The white bark sheds layers like tissue paper and becomes black and rugged at the base.

characters.description: Base of old B. pendula becomes thick, black, deeply fissured with diamond blocks; white above. B. pubescens base much less fissured.
characters.quote: the bark thickens, becoming irregular, dark, and rugged

characters.description: Horizontal peeling of papery thin layers; flammable, oily.
characters.quote: The white bark sheds layers like tissue paper and becomes black and rugged at the base.

characters.description: Dark horizontal lenticel bands; in downy birch bark is dull grey-white with fine lenticels.
characters.quote: smooth but dull grey-white bark finely marked with dark horizontal lenticels

characters.description: B. pubescens: duller, greyer, base less black-fissured, trunk less pendulous crown. Overlap with pendula in saplings - unreliable alone.
characters.quote: greyer, less fissured, in downy birch

characters.description: B. pendula: slender hairless pendulous twigs; B. pubescens branches ascending, never pendulous.
characters.quote: but never pendulous (as with silver birch)

characters.description: B. pendula twigs hairless with resin warts; B. pubescens twigs downy-hairy. Best pendula vs pubescens separator (hand lens/close photo).
characters.quote: Twigs are smooth, and have small dark warts.

characters.description: Small triangular leaves with double-toothed margin; B. pubescens more ovate, single teeth.
characters.quote: Light green, small and triangular-shaped with a toothed edge, which fade to yellow in autumn.

characters.description: B. pubescens favours wet, poorly drained sites; B. pendula dry sandy soil.
characters.quote: more common on wet, poorly drained sites, such as clays and peat bogs

characters.description: Pale, fine uniform diffuse-porous grain, faint reddish-brown heartwood; burns hot, paper-bark often kept on logs (key for firewood).
characters.quote: pale in colour with a light reddish-brown heartwood

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Birch peels in papery horizontal sheets with black lenticel marks; aspen smooth grey-green with diamond lenticels, no peeling.
look_alikes.quote: The white bark sheds layers like tissue paper and becomes black and rugged at the base.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Warty hairless twigs and black fissured base = pendula; downy twigs, greyer bark = pubescens.
look_alikes.quote: hairy and without warts in downy birch

characters.description: A. glutinosa young trees smooth, glossy, greenish-brown with lenticels.
characters.quote: The bark of young trees is smooth, glossy and greenish-brown while in older trees it is dark grey and fissured.

characters.description: A. glutinosa old: dark grey-brown to blackish, fissured into small rectangular plates/blocks; often lichen-covered.
characters.quote: The bark is dark and fissured and is often covered in lichen.

characters.description: A. incana: smooth pale grey bark persisting into old age, only slight fissuring at base; suckers and stump sprouts.
characters.quote: smooth grey bark even in old age

characters.description: Often multi-stemmed/leaning, near water, with adventitious roots at base; crown narrow, sparse with old tree lower branches lost.
characters.quote: The base of the trunk produces adventitious roots

characters.description: A. incana forms thickets via root/stump suckers; many stems of similar age.
characters.quote: vigorous production of stump suckers

characters.description: A. glutinosa buds purplish and stalked, sticky; A. incana buds sessile, grey-hairy (general knowledge).
characters.quote: The purple or grey leaf buds form on long stems.

characters.description: A. glutinosa leaf tip rounded/notched; A. incana leaf pointed, matt, grey underside.
characters.quote: The leaf tip is never pointed and is often indented.

characters.description: Small woody cone-like catkins persisting through winter beside old ones and male catkins.
characters.quote: small brown cones, which are the female catkins and stay on the tree all year round

characters.description: Riparian, swamp, wet forest.
characters.quote: Its natural habitat is moist ground near rivers, ponds and lakes.

characters.description: Freshly cut wood white then rapidly turns pale orange-red; soft, uniform; poor firewood. Decisive for freshly-cut logs.
characters.quote: white when first cut, turning to pale red

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Young alder bark is dull greenish/dark; birch is white; alder cones are woody and persistent.
look_alikes.quote: Alder is the only British native deciduous tree to develop cones.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Smooth grey old bark = incana; dark fissured plates = glutinosa.
look_alikes.quote: smooth grey bark even in old age

characters.description: Smooth, grey, with faint vertical paler streaks; remains thin and smooth in old age, only shallow ridges.
characters.quote: smooth and greenish-grey, even in old trees

characters.description: Pale grey with vertical markings/streaks; older trunks ridged.
characters.quote: Its bark is pale grey with vertical markings.

characters.description: Fluted, sinewy, muscle-like trunk with ridges; often twisted and crooked; main identifier of bark-only photos.
characters.quote: often has a fluted and crooked trunk

characters.description: Short twisted trunk with ridges with age; pollards/coppice stools common.
characters.quote: sometimes a short, twisted trunk which develops ridges with age

characters.description: Dense rounded to ovoid crown, small tree (to 20-25 m), spreading branches; in hedges retains dead leaves.
characters.quote: dense foliage

characters.description: Oval double-serrated leaves with deeply pleated parallel veins (corrugated); beech leaf margin entire.
characters.quote: prominent veins giving a distinctive corrugated texture

characters.description: Short buds pressed against twig and slightly curved at tip; beech buds longer, pointed, divergent.
characters.quote: the leaf buds are similar to beech, only shorter and slightly curved at the tips.

characters.description: Ribbed nutlet with three-pointed leafy bract in hanging clusters.
characters.quote: partly enclosed by a three-pointed leafy involucre

characters.description: Whitish, very hard, heavy, tough, no heartwood contrast, diffuse-porous with wavy irregular rings; outstanding firewood.
characters.quote: heavy and hard

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Hornbeam has fluted, sinewy trunk and smaller crown; beech is round smooth cylindrical and bark more uniformly silver.
look_alikes.quote: often has a fluted and crooked trunk

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Hornbeam buds short and pressed; beech long and cigar-shaped.
look_alikes.quote: pressed close to the twig

characters.description: Thin smooth grey bark that stays smooth even on very large old trunks; often mottled with lichens/algae; no fissures. Best single bark character in the region.
characters.quote: Smooth, thin, and dark gray-blue in color, smooth even on the largest stems, may be mottled.

characters.description: Silver-grey smooth bark, never corky or fissured, at all ages.
characters.quote: Bark silver-grey, smooth, never corky.

characters.description: Horizontal 'eyebrow' creases around branch scars and bulges; very old trees may show shallow vertical cracking (general knowledge).
Stocky straight cylindrical bole in forest stands, clear of branches for a long length; pillar look.
characters.quote: A medium size tree reaching up to 90 feet tall with a stocky trunk and a round crown.

characters.description: Old trunks may show broad buttress-like root flares and slight fluting, much less than hornbeam (general knowledge).
Open-grown trees: short trunk with low massive spreading branches and very broad dense dome crown.
characters.quote: a short trunk with low branches

characters.description: Often a single, slightly sinuous trunk with sinuous limbs.
characters.quote: on a single, often sinuous trunk

characters.description: Winter buds long (about 2.5 cm), cigar-shaped, sharply pointed, diverging from zigzag twig. Highly diagnostic in winter.
characters.quote: buds are long (1 inch), light brown, and slender, covered with overlapping scales that are tinged with tomentum

characters.description: Simple alternate ovate leaf with wavy or nearly entire margin, 7-9 vein pairs.
characters.quote: with a nearly entire to somewhat toothed or wavy margin.

characters.description: Brown dead leaves persist on lower branches through winter.
characters.quote: marcescent below

characters.description: Two triangular nuts in a spiny four-valved husk; litter beneath tree.
characters.quote: Nuts are irregularly triangular, shiny brown and edible, found in pairs within a woody husk

characters.description: Pale straw colour, sometimes pink or brown tint; red heart possible.
characters.quote: Pale straw color, sometimes with a pink or brown hue.

characters.description: Diffuse-porous (sometimes near semi-ring); wide noded rays show as flecks on radial face; no odour.
characters.quote: Rays: Medium to very wide, with normal spacing and "noded" ray structure.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Hornbeam is strongly fluted with sinewy ridges and blotchy bark; beech is round-stocky and uniformly smooth. Beech buds are long, cigar-shaped.
look_alikes.quote: buds are long (1 inch), light brown, and slender, covered with overlapping scales that are tinged with tomentum

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Aspen smooth bark has diamond lenticels and turns black and fissured at base with age; beech never fissures.

characters.description: Grey-brown bark with closely set deep vertical fissures and ridges; rugged on old trees.
characters.quote: The bark is greyish-brown and closely grooved, with vertical plates.

characters.description: Very old oaks have massive deeply furrowed blocky ridges; thick bark.
characters.quote: Bark grey-brown, fissured with short deep ridges.

characters.description: Young trunks smooth shiny grey-brown with faint cracks before fissuring (about 20-30 years); not diagnostic.
Bark of Q. robur and Q. petraea overlaps; petraea tends shallower; unreliable. Use leaves/acorns.
characters.quote: Bark brown-grey with shallow short ridges.

characters.description: Open-grown: spreading unevenly domed crown with massive tortuous lower branches; short bole.
characters.quote: The crown is spreading and unevenly domed, and trees often have massive lower branches.

characters.description: Large burrs on trunk bearing clusters of small shoots.
characters.quote: There are often large burrs on the trunk, which typically produce many small shoots.

characters.description: Masses of epicormic shoots after sudden exposure.
characters.quote: Sudden light exposure can cause masses of epicormic shoots, giving attractive 'cat's paw' figure but weakening timber.

characters.description: Obovate lobed leaf with auricled base and very short petiole (2-7 mm).
characters.quote: They have a cordate (auricled) base and 3–6 rounded lobes,

characters.description: Acorns on long stalks (4-8 cm), clusters of 2-3.
characters.quote: The fruits (acorns) are borne in clusters of 2–3 on a long peduncle (stalk) 4–8 cm long.

characters.description: Blunt multi-scaled buds clustered at shoot tips; alternate.
Ring-porous, large earlywood pores; yellowish-brown heartwood, durable, tannin smell.
characters.quote: Like Sessile Oak, its timber is superior to most, with durable heartwood and high strength.

characters.description: Very wide rays prominent on radial face (silver flecks) and visible on end grain.
characters.quote: rays of two distinct sizes: narrow and very wide, normal spacing; wider rays are visible without magnification

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Pedunculate oak has stalked acorns and short-petiole auricled leaves; sessile oak has stalkless acorns and long petiole.
look_alikes.quote: Pedunculate Oak differs: backward auricles, short petiole, intercalary veins, stalked acorns.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Red oak ridges are smooth with shiny central stripes; robur is rough and deeply fissured.
look_alikes.quote: Bark grey-brown, smooth, developing ridges with distinctive shiny central stripes.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Old ash bark forms a diamond lattice and has opposite black buds; oak has alternate clustered buds.

characters.description: Grey-brown bark, shallower ridges, often straighter than robur; overlapping.
characters.quote: Bark brown-grey with shallow short ridges.

characters.description: More upright straight trunk and straighter branches than robur.
characters.quote: It has a more upright trunk and straighter branches than English oak

characters.description: Upright crown with straight branches vs gnarled spreading robur.
characters.quote: with an upright form and straight branching.

characters.description: Long petiole, wedge-shaped base, regular lobes, no auricles.
characters.quote: on a long petiole (10-25mm).

characters.description: Acorns stalkless; decisive vs robur (hybrids Q. x rosacea exist).
characters.quote: Acorns sessile.

characters.description: Young trunks smooth; not diagnostic.
Same as robur: ring-porous, wide rays, durable brown heartwood.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Petiole length and acorn stalk.
look_alikes.quote: Pedunculate Oak differs: backward auricles, short petiole, intercalary veins, stalked acorns.

characters.description: Smooth-topped flat ridges with shiny silvery central stripes ('ski tracks') running far up the trunk. Strongest bark character; unlike robur's deep rough fissures.
characters.quote: Bark grey-brown, smooth, developing ridges with distinctive shiny central stripes.

characters.description: Young trunk smooth grey; stripes develop later.
Old bark dark reddish-grey, broad rounded ridges, somewhat scaly.
characters.quote: Dark reddish gray brown, with broad, thin, rounded ridges, scaly.

characters.description: Straight bole with straight branches radiating outward; widely planted.
characters.quote: with straight branches radiating outwards.

characters.description: Large (20 cm) leaves with 3-5 pointed bristle-tipped lobes; red autumn colour.
characters.quote: Leaves large (20cm), oval or obovate, with 3-5 pointed, unevenly toothed lobes, dark green and glabrous above

characters.description: Broad acorn in shallow flat cupule; matures second year.
characters.quote: Fruit a small broad acorn (2cm) in a shallow cupule.

characters.description: Pointed reddish-brown buds, hairy-tipped.
characters.quote: Winter buds: Dark chestnut brown (reddish brown), ovate, acute, generally 6 mm (1⁄4 in) long

characters.description: Reddish-brown heartwood, ring-porous with open pores (no tyloses).
characters.quote: Heartwood is a light to medium brown, commonly with a reddish cast.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Red oak: shiny stripes on flat ridges, pointed lobes; robur has rounded lobes, auricles, deep fissures.
look_alikes.quote: Bark grey-brown, smooth, developing ridges with distinctive shiny central stripes.

characters.description: Smooth olive-brown young bark, silvery-grey on older branches.
characters.quote: The bark is smooth, olive-brown when young and silvery-grey on older branches

characters.description: Silver-grey bark with broad scattered fissures and wide flat ridges; paler and more open than black walnut.
characters.quote: Walnut bark is smooth and olive-brown when young, developing fissures and fading to silver-grey with age.

characters.description: Old bark ridged and darkening; sometimes basally burred.
characters.quote: Bark grey and smooth when young, darkening and ridging with age, sometimes basally burred.

characters.description: Diamond pattern may appear on ashy-grey flat ridges but broader and paler than J. nigra; weakly diagnostic.
characters.quote: Light, ashey gray, with flattened ridges, developing a striking diamond shaped pattern.

characters.description: Short stout trunk, broad spreading crown; solitary garden/roadside tree, often leaning.
characters.quote: Large (35m), often leaning, boldly and sparsely branched, broad-crowned.

characters.description: 5-9 smooth-margined leaflets with a terminal leaflet; aromatic.
characters.quote: Leaves pinnate compound, 20-30cm, with 5-9 (usually seven) smooth-margined leaflets, always with a terminal one.

characters.description: Stout twigs with chambered pith (cut a twig lengthwise), large pubescent buds, 3-lobed leaf scar.
characters.quote: Stout, light brown, with a buff-colored chambered pith

characters.description: Round green husk; thin nut with shallow furrows.
characters.quote: nut is relatively thin and smooth with a few shallow furrows

characters.description: Pale sapwood and dark chocolate-brown heartwood.
characters.quote: Exquisite hardwood, with pale sapwood and dark chocolate-brown heartwood

characters.description: Semi-ring-porous with gradual decline in pore size.
characters.quote: large earlywood pores grading to medium latewood pores, few; solitary and radial multiples of 2-3.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: J. nigra has 10-24 serrate leaflets and darker deeply diamond-furrowed bark; regia has 5-9 smooth leaflets and paler bark.
look_alikes.quote: Common walnut has fewer leaflets than black walnut

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Walnut leaves alternate with chambered pith; ash opposite with solid pith.

characters.quote: Brown on surface, darker brown when cut, ridged and furrowed with a rough diamond pattern.

characters.description: Grey-black, deeply furrowed into thin ridges.
characters.quote: The bark is typically grey-black and deeply furrowed into thin ridges that gives the bark a diamond-shaped pattern.

characters.description: Young trunk smooth grey-brown with shallow furrows; not diagnostic.

characters.description: 10-24 serrate leaflets, terminal often missing; aromatic.

characters.quote: buds are tan, and large with a few pubescent scales

characters.description: Chocolate-brown heartwood with darker streaks, pale sapwood; semi-ring porous; faint odour.

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Walnut alternate leaves, chambered pith, darker bark; ash opposite leaves with black buds.
look_alikes.quote: Alternate, pinnately compound, 12 to 24 inches long with 10 to 24 leaflets

look_alikes.how_to_tell: Robinia bark is rope-like and has thorns; black walnut has diamond pattern and large leaves.

characters.description: Pale grey smooth bark with cream lenticels.

characters.quote: Large (35m or more), often slender with a slightly sinuous trunk, though commonly coppiced and pollarded.

characters.description: Pale cream to light brown wood, tough, heavy; olive heartwood sometimes.
